title: Service Uptime Orchestra: Onboarding Roadmap & SLO Implementation (30-60-90)
content:
Purpose and context:
This playbook is an operational onboarding roadmap for the "Service Uptime Orchestra" initiative — an organized program to bring a set of prioritized services into a consistent SLO-driven lifecycle. The focus is cross-functional alignment: product owners, service engineers, platform, observability, and support. This is intentionally pragmatic: lightweight checklists, clear handoffs, and measurable milestones for 30 / 60 / 90 day windows rather than an idealized, multi-month program plan.

Why this exists:
- Reduce variance in how teams define and adopt SLOs for model-serving endpoints and control planes.
- Create repeatable onboarding run (templates, alerting, dashboards, playbooks) so new services can reach an agreed availability/latency bar faster.
- Centralize lessons learned and short feedback loops into Redwood Console integrations (dashboards, alerts).

Goals (measurable):
1) Within 90 days, onboard 6 services to the standard SLO profile (availability + P95 latency), with documented owners and runbook.
2) Reduce number of P1 incidents caused by misconfigured alert thresholds by 30% for onboarded services.
3) Ensure every onboarded service has automated telemetry (SLO metrics, error budgets, traces) ingested into the Console.

Scope (what this playbook covers):
In-scope:
- Defining service SLOs (availability and latency profiles)
- Instrumentation checklist for metrics/traces
- Alerting templates with clear escalation paths
- Runbook and postmortem template adoption
- Cross-functional onboarding rituals (kickoff, cadence, handoff)
Out-of-scope:
- Re-architecture decisions to change service topology (those get separate eng tickets)

Stakeholders and roles:
- Program lead: Priya Nair (program coordination, status)
- SRE partner: Jordan Chen (SLO design review, runbook signoff)
- Observability: Aisha Malik (dashboard templates, metric contracts)
- Platform/Infra: Luca Moretti (ingest quotas, retention config, RBAC for dashboards)
- Product liaison: Sam Rodriguez (customer impact, release gating)
- Customer Success: optional reviewer on customer-impact language

Definition of Done (for a single service):
- SLO document exists in the service repo and Confluence (availability and latency numeric targets).
- SLO metrics are emitted and visible in Console within 48 hours of enabling instrumentation.
- Error budget metric is computed and an alert is created for budget burn rate > threshold.
- Runbook with step-by-step mitigation is published and linked from oncall dashboard.
- Postmortem template used for first production incident after onboarding.

30/60/90 day cadence (detailed):
Days 0-30 (Discover & Instrument)
- Week 0: Intake kickoff (15–30 min) with service owner + SRE + Observability. Kickoff checklist: current SLAs, traffic patterns, customer-visible endpoints, and owner contact list. (Owner: Priya)
- Week 1: Baseline analysis: export 30-day metrics (availability, latency distribution, error rates) and capture current alert noise. (Owner: Observability)
- Week 2: SLO proposal draft — recommended availability and latency SLOs with justification (traffic, customer criticality, cost sensitivity). Light-weight PR to service repo. (Owner: Jordan)
- Week 3–4: Add/validate instrumentation (metrics + traces). Confirm metrics in Console; create initial dashboards. (Owner: Aisha)
Deliverables by day 30: SLO draft PR, instrumentation validation, kickoff notes and baseline snapshot.

Days 31-60 (Stabilize & Alerting)
- Week 5: Review SLO proposal with product liaison. Finalize numeric targets and agree on error budget policy (escalation thresholds, automated throttles if any). (Owner: Priya + Sam)
- Week 6: Implement alerting templates: budget burn rate alert, availability drop alert, P95 latency regression alert. Ensure low-noise thresholds to avoid fatigue. (Owner: Jordan)
- Week 7: Runbook creation and play simulation. Runbooks must include: how to check ingress/egress, how to roll back model or rollout, mitigation steps for caching/kv issues, and communications templates. (Owner: Service owner + SRE)
- Week 8: Dry-run tabletop on most likely failure mode. Capture runbook gaps. (Owner: SRE)
Deliverables by day 60: final SLO document merged, dashboard and alerts live, published runbook, tabletop notes with remediation backlog.

Days 61-90 (Operationalize & Handoff)
- Week 9: Observe error budget consumption under real traffic; adjust thresholds if necessary. Tag any noisy alerts for refinement. (Owner: Observability + Service)
- Week 10: Handoff to oncall rotation: ensure oncall engineers know where to find SLOs, runbooks, and escalation contacts. Update oncall run cadence if needed. (Owner: SRE lead)
- Week 11: Post-onboard review meeting: 30-minute review with product, service, and SRE. Agree on maintenance cadence and who will own SLO reviews every quarter. (Owner: Priya)
- Week 12: Close onboarding ticket and publish a short retro (what worked, blockers, follow-ups). Archive artifacts. (Owner: Priya)
Deliverables by day 90: oncall signoff, retro published, ticket closed, plan for quarterly SLO review scheduled.

Cross-functional rituals and meeting templates:
- Intake kickoff template (agenda): 10m intro, 15m baseline metrics, 10m target risk discussion, 5m next steps.
- Weekly 30-min sync during onboarding with strict note-taking and action owners.
- Tabletop template for dry-run: scope scenario, runbook walk, decision tree walk-through, timebox 45 mins.
- Postmortem template: timeline, impact, detection, mitigation, action items (owner + ETA), follow-up review scheduled.

Engineering artifacts and quick links to standardize:
- SLO YAML template (repo): location: /deploy/slo.yaml (fields: name, target_availability, latency_p95_ms, measurement_window_days).
- Alert rules repo: /ops/alerts/common (reference PR examples in linked_artifacts).
- Dashboard starter: Console > Templates > SLO-Onboard-Starter.

Operational playbook excerpts (short):
- If availability drops below threshold: 1) check rollout/versions, 2) check model health (if applicable), 3) switch traffic to canary/previous revision, 4) notify customers via status page.
- If P95 latency regresses > 2x baseline: 1) identify recent deploys (tag), 2) examine KV-cache hit rates, 3) throttle batch sizes or fall back to smaller model variant, 4) open mitigation PR.

Dependencies and open questions:
- Console quota limits and retention for high-cardinality SLO tags (Platform/Infra dependency).
- Agreement on default SLO templates for low-, medium-, and high-priority services (Product decision).
- Ticket to add standard SLO YAML parser to CI to validate format (engineering task: RED-3120).

Risk register (top items):
- Risk: Alert fatigue from overly aggressive error-budget alerts. Mitigation: phase-in thresholds, test with synthetic burn before enabling in prod.
- Risk: Instrumentation gaps across languages / runtimes. Mitigation: library adapters + checklist for each runtime.
- Risk: Ownership ambiguity after handoff. Mitigation: require oncall signoff and quarterly SLO review assignment at close.

Metrics & reporting (how we know we succeeded):
- Number of services onboarded per quarter (target: 6/quarter).
- Time from kickoff to SLO merge (median target: <= 45 days).
- Alert noise: #alerts/week per service (target: <3 noisy alerts/week).
- P1 incident reduction for onboarded services vs. baseline.

Templates and artifacts to create next (owners):
- SLO YAML validator in CI: (Owner: Platform, ticket RED-3120)
- Onboarding checklist in Confluence (Owner: Priya)
- Dashboard and alert templates per priority profile (Owner: Aisha)
- Library adapters for Go/Python/Java runtimes (Owner: Platform Engineering)

Close-out and continuous improvement:
- After each onboarded service, capture 3 quick lessons (what saved time, what tripped us, what to improve) into the central playbook.
- Monthly program retro: 30 minutes to identify recurring blockers (instrumentation, alerts, ownership).
- Quarterly review: re-evaluate default SLO templates and error budget policy across product lines.

Appendix: quick meeting notes (sample from intake 2026-02-18)
- Service: embeddings-cache
- Baseline: 99.6% 30-day availability (incidents due to eviction storms)
- Proposed SLO: 99.9% availability; P95 latency 180ms
- Action items: add eviction metrics to Console (Aisha, 3 days), draft SLO PR (service owner, 5 days), schedule tabletop after instrumentation.

Next steps (for Priya):
1) Open program tracker ticket (linear RED-3001) and add 6 candidate services.
2) Schedule onboarding slots for next four weeks and publish the intake calendar.
3) Convene quick alignment with Platform to confirm Console quotas.

Document history:
- 2026-02-12: initial draft created (Priya)
- 2026-02-18: intake template updated after first pilot
- 2026-03-03: added 30/60/90 deliverables and appendix notes
